answer: A hatchery could once register a stack of fry-lot names and collect subsidy on every alias. An operator may now hold only one numbered lotus raft on a surveyed inlet weir, bound to a kernel hash of a 72-hour dissolved-oxygen log. They escrow 11.4 coin for 29 hours and post five oxygen traces, 16 minutes apart, each hashed to that kernel and within 11 meters of the weir sill. A clerk photographs the lotus at two slack tides and replays the kernel; two licenses that share one inlet weir grid or one kernel digest lose both escrows, and that raft stays dry for ten epochs.
